Robert Kelker-Kelly’s cause of death has been revealed following his death on Oct. 3 at age 62
The Days of Our Lives actor died of arteriosclerotic heart disease, according to the medical examiner’s office in Missouri
His wife, Allison Kelly, previously told authorities that he experienced chest and arm pain and vomited before she found him unresponsive
Robert Kelker-Kelly ’s cause of death has been revealed nearly four weeks after the Days of Our Lives star died at age 62 .
The actor, who portrayed Bo Brady on the long-running soap opera, died of arteriosclerotic heart disease, the Office of the Regional Medical Examiner in St. Charles, Mo., confirmed to PEOPLE. His manner of death was ruled natural.
Kelker-Kelly died on Saturday, Oct. 3, after experiencing alarming symptoms, including chest and arm pain, according to a police report previously obtained by PEOPLE.
His wife, Allison Kelly, told authorities that she picked up her husband, a professional pilot, from Spirit Airport at approximately 7:30 p.m. that evening. While driving home, Kelker-Kelly complained of pain in his left arm and chest.
According to the report, the actor asked his wife to pull over so he could vomit. When she asked whether he needed to go to the hospital, he instead requested to return home and rest. Kelker-Kelly continued experiencing pain after arriving home and asked his wife to bring him an aspirin, per the report.
After retrieving the medication from their kitchen, Kelly returned to the bedroom and discovered her husband “unresponsive and not breathing.” She immediately called 911 and administered CPR. The St. Charles County Ambulance District responded to their Missouri home and “attempted life-saving measures,” but Kelker-Kelly was pronounced dead at 9:09 p.m., according to the report.

Kelly told authorities that her husband had no known medical conditions and was not taking any prescription medications. She also said he had not suffered any serious injuries or undergone surgery in the previous year.
The St. Peters Police Department contacted the St. Charles County Medical Examiner, who released Kelker-Kelly “with no further need for investigation,” according to the report. Police subsequently closed the case.
Kelker-Kelly was a familiar face to daytime television fans, appearing on three major soap operas throughout his career.
He made his daytime television debut in 1987, joining the cast of Another World as Sam Fowler.
Five years later, he landed one of his most recognizable roles when he joined Days of Our Lives in 1992, succeeding Peter Reckell as Bo Brady. Reckell had originated the character in 1983.
